In summary, our research is concerned with
the initiation of dorso- ventral axis formation during chick limb development, using the chick as a model.
how the limb-forming region of the chick embryo is defined and what factors contribute to this process.
how FGFs initiate dorso-ventrally patterned limb mesoderm in chick embryos.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Wnt- 7a expression is the earliest and most direct response of the ectoderm to FGF-2, whereas Lmx-1 is a later and more indirect response of the mesoderm.
Wnt-1a expression is necessary for limb formation, but not sufficient to induce a limb, and that the FGF-8 gene is necessary and sufficient to induce a normal limb.
the FGF-7/FGF-10/Wnt-7a/Lmx-1/Fgf-8 cascade is the key pathway in dorso-ventrally patterning limb mesoderm during limb formation in chick.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dorso-ventrally asymmetric gene expression in limb-forming mesoderm is induced in response to FGF signalling from the dorsal ectoderm.
the FGF-induced limb bud has an intrinsic dorso-ventrally patterned mesoderm and that the dorsal ectoderm is induced by FGFs to produce Wnt-7, which then signals to the mesoderm.
FGF-2 is the first signal that induces limb-forming ectoderm and mesoderm, and that Wnt- 7a expression in dorsal ectodermal cells is an early event in this induction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the molecular events that lead to dorso-vental axis formation during chick limb development are similar to those in the mouse but that the kinetics and patterns of gene expression are different.
FGF-2 application to flank mesoderm can induce Wnt-7 expression and that Wnt-8 is required for limb induction in the chick.

Wnt- 7a is an early marker of dorsal ectoderm and is induced by FGF-2 application to the flank and that Lmx-1 is induced in dorsal mesodermal cells by FGF- 2 application, probably through an intermediate Wnt-7 signalling.
